newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade shrugs off Thai news.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade shrugs off Thai news.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Monday with most players shrugging off news the Thai government had intervened in the market to prop up prices, dealers said.
"People in the market were looking more at the spot expiry in Japan and they were sidelined because of holidays in New York and London," a trader said.
"I don't think it had any real impact in the market. I've seen no shift among buyers here in favour of Indonesia and against Thailand," a trader said.

Firmer prices in the Tokyo and Kobe rubber markets may give prices a boost in the afternoon session. "We're just waiting for some leads from the Japanese market this afternoon. There was nothing traded this morning," a dealer said.
The trade also shook off reports of a riot in Banjarmasin which shut down rubber factories in the South Kalimantan city.

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 was indicated at 115.50 U.S. cents a kg from 113.00 cents. July RSS1 was indicated at 163.00-165.00 Singapore cents (US$1.14-$1.15) a kg from 161.50 cents. July TSR20 was indicated at 156.50 Singapore cents (US$1.09) a kg from 154.75 cents. - (S$1.43 = US$1) Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
